subject: iOS shell is broken for the owner; your PR #385 merges first, the cloud repair batch is re-based on it; the build, the negative check and the device run are yours
body:
MERGE ORDER FIRST. Your PR #385 (mac/native-ledger-2026-09-02 @ 84b0e85) merges BEFORE the cloud batch. The batch was rebuilt on the post-merge tree (579d316 + 84b0e85; the auto-merge was clean, then five files conflicted with the batch — BackendService, BadgeReaderProvider, IdentityProvider, DeviceInfo, PROVIDER_CONFIGURATION.md — and were resolved by hand with both sides read in full). Where both lanes fixed the same defect your compiled mechanism won: DeviceInfo's compiled-out MDM facts (my in-memory identifier cache is layered on), HybridIdentityProvider assign-after-await verbatim, SecurityManager's attestation-beside-key, one usbC = "usbc" case in your spelling, your six dead-stored-property removals, and your route-absence provenance comments carried into the BackendService rewrite — whose tri-state configuration (configured | refused | absent), served-contract session start/end with the decision honoured, ControlPlaneSessionIdentityProvider, local audit and enrollment refusal are the final shape. Your two SecurityManager findings are fixed in the same batch: X-Device-Binding is SHA-256 of the key (never the key); token binding carries its mint timestamp and verifyTokenBinding recomputes from the same inputs and compares in constant time; a comment and a README 'Backend API' row say no server route reads those headers yet. Your check-ios-dead-stored-properties gate stays; the two cloud gates append after it in preflight and CI. ProviderConfigurationService's new managed backend key is spelled BackendBaseURL so it is the key KioskConfig actually reads. NOTHING in the batch has met a compiler; that is what the sim request below is for.

WHY. The owner ran the app and said it is broken. A cloud read found why, all in non-parity files, and the repair batch lands as a PR after yours, with sim-request artifacts/sim-requests/2026-09-02-ios-shell-repair.json (runs: ios-shell-repair, everything-fast). What changed: (1) LockedIdle was a dead screen on a phone: the keyboard-wedge provider listened for a notification nothing posted, Manual login was hidden without managed AllowManualOverride, the status line read the legacy BadgeReaderManager. Now a hidden first-responder captures HID input; on an UNMANAGED phone the holder turns on "Allow local sign-in on this unmanaged device" in iOS Settings → Enterprise Shell (Settings.bundle key local_session_allowed, default off), and the code-free path additionally requires the ASAM probe to read unavailable (not-attempted refuses; an engaged kiosk lock proves supervision whatever the app-config dictionary says). AllowManualOverride defaults to false everywhere; absent policy is never permission. Two independent reviews drove that shape; the first cut had inferred "unmanaged" from a missing app-config dictionary, which a supervised device without an app-config payload also satisfies. (2) project.yml pinned an empty DEVELOPMENT_TEAM and the entitlements demanded associated-domains, an app group, notifications and a keychain access group the code never used; entitlements emptied, signing via tracked native/ios/Signing.xcconfig ending in #include? "Signing.local.xcconfig" (untracked; example committed; put your team and bundle id there). (3) BackendService pointed at a placeholder host; on top of your three path fixes it is rewritten to /api/v1/sessions/start {identityRef, deviceRef, workflowKey} → {session, decision}, only an allow starts a session; base URL resolves managed BackendBaseURL → -DemoBackendURL (simulator, loopback only) → BACKEND_BASE_URL → absent; every consumer tightens on refused; the fatalError on http is a thrown error permitting loopback only (the AuditLogger's 30 s timer used to hit it even in demo); audit stays local with a bounded queue because the server has no ingest route (your enumeration is quoted in the code); enrollment says plainly the backend cannot enroll. (4) OIDC placeholder tenant force-unwrapped a URL (crash on refresh); AppLauncher called UIApplication off-main and force-unwrapped a server-supplied bundle id. (5) the fake Refresh toast. Companion gates: check-ios-policy-defaults (a managedBool default derived from management state fails) and check-sim-scripts-selfcheck.

WHAT ONLY YOU CAN DO, in order, after both PRs are on Alpha: ./scripts/mac/ios-shell-repair.sh --self-check (must exit 0 without Xcode), then the real run: xcodegen generate, build for iPhone 17 AND -sdk iphoneos CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO (the DeviceInfo #else branches), demo launch, no-flag launch with the toggle OFF (the lock-screen audit line must read manual_login_available=false), toggle ON via defaults write com.enterprise.shell local_session_allowed -bool true and relaunch (must read true), -DemoBackendURL http://127.0.0.1:8080 against a running api-server with a 40 s soak, the accessibility-extra-large screenshot, then the NEGATIVE once: temporarily set allowManualOverride's default to true and confirm step 5a FAILS (that is what proves the checker is not vacuous; revert). Confirm Settings.bundle appears in iOS Settings on the simulator. Commit the sim-result and the screenshots. If anything fails to compile, name the file:line in the result; the cloud fixes it. Device build with your team in Signing.local.xcconfig stays a note. Unrelated: scripts/mac/run-everything.sh gained the guarded empty-array idiom on its SUMMARY loop in #374; behaviour-preserving on every path you take. Owner note 2026-09-02 14:5x: Docker Desktop is running on the Mac (postgres:16, redis:7, fleetdm/fleet, nginx, traccar, envoy present; the two signalgrid-review-hub images are 26 days old, so rebuild before relying on them). That unblocks the Postgres and Fleet live lanes and the local api-server on 8080 for the iOS soak step; run the ios-shell-repair operation with the api-server up.
